record.title: San Marino physically closes secondary roads at its Italian border during COVID-19
record.scope: Secondary border roads physically blocked; main controlled routes preserved
record.crossings: Minor roads along Italian frontier; initially Dogana, Gualdicciolo, Faetano, Cerbaiola and Chiesanuova retained; Rovereta later added with limits
record.movement: Users of secondary roads; no complete isolation of San Marino.
record.exceptions: Main routes remained; Rovereta later admitted heavy vehicles and health staff under time limits.
record.imposing_authority: San Marino civil protection and Secretary of State for Internal Affairs, coordinated with nearby Italian authorities
record.enforcement: Barriers/signs ordered; contemporary report confirms route restrictions.
record.relationship: Promotes physical-road component of EU-L004. Distinct from Italy’s national admission regime R3-EU-003; Monaco part of lead remains unresolved.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Limit and monitor cross-border movement to contain COVID-19.
record.context: Physical access reduction channelled permitted travel through staffed routes. May 19 ordinance revoked the remaining road-closure order.
record.uncertainty: Progressive implementation means no all-road first closure instant. Retrospective Gendarmerie summary gives 21 March–3 May and seven routes, conflicting with specific dated instruments; operational endpoint not directly observed.

historical.duration_note: Formal permission or repeal; operational continuity and first physical reopening are not established. Phased closures/exemptions and unresolved retrospective discrepancy; May 19 is formal reopening order only.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Official closure instructions, local closure report and retrospective policing account support physical secondary-road closure.
March 23 progressive closure notice; retrospective March 21 differs and remains contested.
May 19 order immediately reopens affected roads; removal not directly observed.
